release_slices.name: POS logical terminal shift opening
release_slices.plain_english_purpose: Let authorized DGFY admins and cashiers open a POS shift from any logged-in device when they select an active terminal assigned to an allowed location.
release_slices.purpose: Let authorized DGFY admins and cashiers open a POS shift from any logged-in device when they select an active terminal assigned to an allowed location.
release_slices.implementation_summary: Removes physical-device pairing as a required blocker for POS shift opening and checkout while preserving DGFY identity, accepted company membership, active tenant user profile, POS permission, active logical terminal, terminal location binding, location grants, and open-shift controls. Retained pairing endpoints remain compatibility or hardware-specific state.
included_features: Shift opening from any logged-in device for authorized DGFY POS operators
Checkout use-case no longer blocked by missing or stale pairing cookie
Logical terminal readiness copy in POS setup and terminal operations
Governed ADR, API, UAT, and compliance contract updates
excluded_features: PayMongo, payment, billing, settlement, or QR Ph changes
Hardware drawer, receipt print, fiscal print, void, Z-reading, or shift-close pairing rules
Production secrets, controller configuration, or deployment script changes
Unrelated local inventory, CSV import, and error-handler edits from the original dirty checkout
release_slices.regression_warning_summary: This POS release changes the shift-open and checkout authorization path. A regression could either block legitimate operators from opening shifts or allow a POS action without the intended terminal/location/open-shift checks.
potentially_affected_existing_behaviors: POS shift opening for admins and cashiers
POS checkout creation after terminal unlock
Terminal registry validation and location grant enforcement
evidence_covering_regression_risk: Backend POS use-case test proves active logical terminals can open shifts without pairing cookies and inactive or unauthorized terminal/location cases fail closed.
Frontend POS contract tests prove TerminalPage no longer imports pairing as the unlock authority and preserves terminal selection copy.
POS reconciliation integration test harness now seeds active logical terminal registry state for direct checkout use-case calls.
Architecture, docs, compliance, and POS production build checks passed on the clean release branch.
evidence_gaps: No seeded staging or production DGFY cashier/admin end-to-end mutation UAT has been run for this exact release SHA.
Rendered local proof reached the DGFY terminal login screen; post-login terminal selection copy remains credential/session-gated.
Full backend matrix and full frontend suite must be confirmed by GitHub CI after the follow-up test-fixture update.
rollback_or_monitoring_notes: Rollback by reverting this release commit and redeploying through the same governed flow.
Monitor POS shift-open failures, terminal-location denial reason codes, checkout creation failures, and pairing-cookie related 401 responses after deployment.

documentation_closure.rationale: The implementation stays inside existing POS, DGFY, Users, and Settings boundaries but changes the governed POS authorization contract, so the accepted POS ADR, DGFY ADR, API spec, UAT checklist, feature journey, and compliance declaration were updated together.

documents.evidence: Documents that POS shift opening and checkout require logical terminal, permission, location, and open-shift authority, not a physical pairing cookie.
Clarifies that POS use is authorized from any logged-in device through DGFY membership, permissions, logical terminal, and location grants.
Records the accepted logical-terminal shift-open contract and preserves pairing only as optional compatibility state.
Declares the POS-sensitive authorization change, excluded payment scope, compliance risk, validation, and rollback notes.
Updates POS journey wording so terminal identity at unlock is the active logical terminal assigned to an allowed location.
Updates the DGFY POS control matrix to test logical terminal access instead of unpaired-device denial.
Updates UAT prerequisites and expected behavior for shift opening from any logged-in device with an active logical terminal.

release_slices.adr_or_compliance: ADR 0031 and ADR 0028 were updated because this release changes the governed POS shift-open authorization contract; a compliance declaration records POS-sensitive scope and explicitly excludes payment-sensitive changes.
release_slices.rollback_notes: Revert this release commit as one unit, rebuild POS, rerun POS backend/frontend tests, architecture, docs lint, compliance, and whitespace checks, then redeploy through the governed controller flow.
